original_target.title: Does a one-cusped finite-volume real hyperbolic manifold exist above dimension four?

full_original_statement: Is there a complete finite-volume **real** hyperbolic $`n`$-manifold with exactly **one cusp** for any $`n\geq5`$? The broader dimension-by-dimension question asks for which such $`n`$ one exists.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual theorem constructs cusp-transitive real hyperbolic4-manifolds with specified cusp sections, not one-cusped n>=5 manifolds. Its introduction expressly retains existence above4 as unknown; a cusp-transitive manifold may have several cusps and a one-cusped reflectofold is a manifold with corners before mirroring. Complex-hyperbolic dimension2 and arithmetic-orbifold exclusions are different classes. No matching higher-dimensional real one-cusp example or general nonexistence claim found.
